 Shri Chitransh Shrivastava - Advocate for the applicant  Ms.Nalini Gurung - P.L. appearing on behalf of responde  ORDER

This is second bail application filed on behalf of applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
2.

The applicant is in jail since 30.07.2023 in connection with Crime No.209 of 2017 registered at P.S. Udaipura, District-Raisen for the offence punishable under Sections 336, 363, 376-A, 366-A &
34 of the IPC and Sections 3, 4 , 5 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
3. Prosecution story in brief is that applicant kidnapped both the minor prosecutrix.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 30.07.2025.
Other co-accused have been acquitted by the trial Court.
It is also urged that both the prosecutrix and their father have been examined and they have turned hostile.
They did not identified present applicant.
Thus, there is no evidence to connect applicant with the instant offence.
On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be released on bail.
5. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55735 2 MCRC-46239-2025 opposed the application.

sentences.text: 6. Looking to aforesaid facts of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
8. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
9. Soft copy of this bail order be sent immediately/forthwith to the applicant through concerned Jail Superintendent.
10. M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
11. Certified copy as per rules.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE sm Govind Rajput vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46695904/
